resources.string: WaveHeaven keeps one summary per minute of listening: how loud your music and your surroundings were. Never audio. It stays on this device and is not included in backups. Summaries older than 30 days are deleted automatically.
Your daily and weekly dose will start again from zero. This cannot be undone.
40 hours a week at 80 dB(A). Recommended for adults.
40 hours a week at 75 dB(A). For children, teenagers or anyone who wants a stricter limit.
You gave consent on %1$s (version %2$d). WaveHeaven may measure while adaptive volume is on.
You have not given consent, so WaveHeaven does not measure anything. You can still see your dose and explore safe listening times.
We updated how WaveHeaven handles your data. Review it and give consent again before adaptive volume can resume.
WaveHeaven will stop measuring at once. Your listening data stays on this device unless you delete it.
Consent withdrawn and listening data deleted
A notification, with vibration and no sound, when you reach a share of your weekly budget, with a tip on what to do.
WaveHeaven adapts the volume of one app on this computer. Choose the one you listen to music with; start it playing if it is not listed.
No app is playing audio right now.

Microphones differ. If you have a sound-level meter (or a calibrated meter app on another phone), put it next to this device in a steady noise, compare its reading with the noise level WaveHeaven shows while adaptive volume runs, and correct the difference here. This only changes how loud WaveHeaven thinks it is around you, never your safe-listening limit.
A five-minute check of how well you hear different pitches in each ear. Not a diagnosis; the result stays on this device.
